dialog.body: Utilities billing, this is Tony. How can I help you?

Hi Tony, yeah, good morning, still morning for another few minutes. My name is Gino DeLuca. So I'm calling for my mother, she's in her eighties, she's had the same account for, oh, going on forty years, and she gets the water and sewer bill in the mail, and I sort of look after the paperwork for her now. I live about twenty minutes away, I come by on Sundays, and this last bill was sitting on the counter.
Okay, sure. Is there something on the bill you're looking at?

Right, right, I'm getting to it. The bill is higher than the last couple, and she's the only one in the house. So what I want is a breakdown of the usage by month. Like month by month for the past year, so I can set up a budget for her. She's on a fixed income and I'd like to know what to expect.
Sure, we can do that. Is the account in her name? I'll need to pull it up by name or account number.
It's in her name, Rosa DeLuca. I don't have the account number in front of me, I left the bill at her house. Is the name enough?

The name should work. Let me look. [pause] Okay, I've got her. So just so you know, our meters are read and billed on a cycle, so it's not necessarily every month. Some of those are quarterly periods. I can give you the usage for each billing period over the last year, and you can divide it out for a monthly figure.
Okay, that makes sense. So it's not twelve separate numbers, it's like four.

Could be four, could be a few more depending on how it was billed. The usage is in units, and the bill shows the charge for water and the charge for sewer separately. Sewer is based on the water that went through the meter.

Okay, so the sewer follows the water. Got it. Now, can you send me a duplicate copy of this latest bill by email? Because I'd rather not wait on the mail, and she's not going to find the paper one anyway, she puts things in drawers.
I can do that. What email address would you like it sent to?
Um, it's gino dot deluca, the number forty-two, at a mail dot com. Sorry, spell that out. G-I-N-O, dot, D-E-L-U-C-A, four two, at a-mail dot com.
Let me read that back. Gino dot Deluca four two at a-mail dot com. That right?
That's it, that's right.
Great. I'll send the duplicate bill and put the usage history together with it. It might take until later today or Monday.

Monday's fine. Now, here's the other thing. The charge itself seems high to me. I looked at the last four bills she had in the drawer, and this one jumped. I'm not saying anything's wrong, but I would like a supervisor to review the charge. Can you put that through, or can I talk to somebody?

Yeah, I can note it for a supervisor review. Sometimes a jump like that is an estimated read, or a leak, like a running toilet. I can see this one was read, not estimated. I can't say why it's up from here, so a supervisor can look at the meter readings. Do you want a call back at a number?
Yes, the number is four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-two. That's my landline.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-two. Got it. And I'll put in the note that you're calling on behalf of your mother, Rosa.
Yes, please. And does she need to say it's okay for me to talk to you? I should have asked that at the start.
For general billing questions we're fine. If there's a change to the account, she might need to sign off or call herself. For now, you're good.

Okay. Also I should tell you, the best way to reach her is not the phone. She doesn't pick up half the time. She gets her news only from the radio in the kitchen, she keeps it on all day, so if she doesn't hear it there, it doesn't reach her. So call me, not her.
Understood, call you at that number. I'll make that note.
Perfect. So to go over it, you're sending the duplicate by email, with the usage by billing period, and a supervisor will review the charge and call me.
That's it exactly. Supervisor should reach out within a few business days.
Okay, that's all I needed. Thanks, Tony.
You're welcome. Have a good weekend.
You too. Bye.
